title: The Atlas gives conflicting units for the sUSDe cooldownShares return value that a rate limit is charged against
content:
Two sections document the same three lines of code and disagree about what they mean.

A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.10.6.2 says the call is made "and the returned `cooldownAmount` of **USDe assets** is decoded from the result", with A...2.1.2.10.6.3 adding that "the resulting `cooldownAmount` of USDe is only known after the cooldown is initiated" and is used to decrease `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN`.

A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.4.2.3.2.2.1 says the operator must decode the result "into a `uint256` value, representing the amount of **shares** that were actually cooled down (`cooldownAmount`)", and A...4.2.3.2.3 then decreases the same `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN` by it.

This is not a cosmetic wording difference. sUSDe is a yield-bearing share, so shares and assets diverge and the gap widens over time. `cooldownAssetsSUSDe` unambiguously debits the same key in USDe (A...4.2.3.1.2), so if the shares reading is correct then one rate-limit key is being charged in two different units depending on which entry point a relayer chooses — and the share-denominated charge would understate the exposure by the accrued yield factor.

The assets reading is the one consistent with the sibling function and with a limit that is supposed to be interpretable over time, so the instance-level text is most likely the error. But a reader of the Artifact alone cannot resolve it, and this is precisely the sort of ambiguity that duplicated documentation produces.
description: The general procedure calls the decoded value the resulting USDe assets; the instance procedure calls it the amount of shares actually cooled down — yet both debit the same LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN key.
